messages.content: What is the equivalent note of C in Indian musical scale? And convert the frequency 440 Hz to wavelength?

function.name: frequency_to_wavelength
function.description: Converts the frequency of a musical note to its wavelength. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

frequency.description: The frequency in hertz of the musical note. This is a float type value.

function.name: note_conversion_indian
function.description: Converts a note in Western music to Indian classical music. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

note.description: The note in Western musical scale.

message.reasoning: The user asks two things: 1) Equivalent note of C in Indian musical scale. 2) Convert frequency 440 Hz to wavelength. We have a tool for frequency_to_wavelength. We need to call that tool. Also we can answer the note conversion manually or use note_conversion_indian tool. The user didn't ask to convert note to Indian scale but asked "What is the equivalent note of C in Indian musical scale?" That is a note conversion. We can use note_conversion_indian tool. So we need to call both tools. The user wants the equivalent note of C in Indian musical scale. That is a direct mapping: C corresponds to Sa (Shadja). So we can answer that. Then we need to convert 440 Hz to wavelength. We need to call frequency_to_wavelength with frequency=440. The speed of sound is 343 m/s. Wavelength = speed / frequency = 343 / 440 = 0.7795 m. So we can compute that. But we should use the tool. The tool will likely compute it. So we need to call frequency_to_wavelength with frequency=440. Then we can provide the result. The user didn't specify the speed of sound, but the tool might assume 343 m/s. So we call the tool.
